content: When the angel of the LORD came, what was Gideon doing in a winepress?
explanation: He was hiding from the Midianites. “where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.” (Judges 6:11, BSB)

content: What did the angel of the LORD call Gideon when he first appeared?
explanation: God saw what Gideon could become. “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.” (Judges 6:12, BSB)

content: What did Gideon put on the threshing floor to test God's promise?
explanation: He asked for a sign with dew. “I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor.” (Judges 6:37, BSB)

content: Before fighting Midian, what did God tell Gideon about his army?
explanation: Israel must not boast it saved itself. “You have too many people for Me to deliver Midian into their hands” (Judges 7:2, BSB)

content: How many men lapped the water and stayed in Gideon's army?
explanation: God saved Israel with a small band. “And the number of those who lapped the water with their hands to their mouths was three hundred men” (Judges 7:6, BSB)

content: Besides a ram's horn, what did each of Gideon's men carry?
options: A jar with a torch inside
explanation: They broke the jars at night. “gave each man a ram’s horn in one hand and a large jar in the other, containing a torch.” (Judges 7:16, BSB)

content: What did Gideon's three hundred men shout around the Midianite camp?
options: A sword for the LORD and Gideon!
explanation: Then the enemy fled. “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!” (Judges 7:20, BSB)

content: When Gideon's men blew horns and broke jars, what did the Midianite army do?
explanation: God gave the victory. “and the entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran.” (Judges 7:21, BSB)

content: Before Samson was born, what did the angel say must never touch his head?
explanation: He was a Nazirite from birth. “And no razor shall come over his head” (Judges 13:5, BSB)

content: Which enemies would Samson begin to save Israel from?
explanation: The angel told his mother. “and he will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.” (Judges 13:5, BSB)

content: When a young lion roared at Samson, what did he do?
explanation: The Spirit came on him powerfully. “and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands” (Judges 14:6, BSB)

content: What was the name of the woman Samson loved in the Valley of Sorek?
explanation: The Philistines paid her to trick him. “Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.” (Judges 16:4, BSB)

content: What did Samson finally tell Delilah was the secret of his strength?
explanation: He was a Nazirite to God. “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.” (Judges 16:17, BSB)

content: While Samson was in prison, what began to grow back?
explanation: His strength would return. “However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.” (Judges 16:22, BSB)

content: At the end, what did Samson push on to bring down the Philistine temple?
explanation: He prayed for strength once more. “And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple.” (Judges 16:29, BSB)

content: In the time of the Judges, whom did the LORD raise up to save Israel?
explanation: They rescued Israel from raiders. “Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.” (Judges 2:16, BSB)

content: Which prophetess was judging Israel when Barak led the army?
explanation: She sat under a palm tree. “Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.” (Judges 4:4, BSB)

content: How does the book of Judges describe Israel when there was no king?
explanation: It was a time of trouble. “In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.” (Judges 21:25, BSB)

content: Where did Deborah sit when Israelites came to her for judgment?
explanation: It was in the hill country of Ephraim. “And she would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel” (Judges 4:5, BSB)

content: What did Barak say to Deborah before going to battle?
options: I'll go only if you go
explanation: Deborah agreed to go with him. “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.” (Judges 4:8, BSB)

content: Deborah told Barak that the enemy commander Sisera would fall into whose hand?
explanation: Barak would get no honor. “because the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a woman.” (Judges 4:9, BSB)

content: To which mountain did Deborah tell Barak to march with ten thousand men?
explanation: God would draw out Sisera. “Go and march to Mount Tabor” (Judges 4:6, BSB)

content: When God called Gideon, what did He tell him to go in?
explanation: God was sending him. “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?” (Judges 6:14, BSB)

content: Why did Gideon say he could not save Israel?
options: He was the youngest of a weak clan
explanation: God promised to be with him. “my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.” (Judges 6:15, BSB)

content: In Gideon's first test, how much water did he wring from the fleece?
explanation: Only the fleece was wet. “he squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew—a bowlful of water.” (Judges 6:38, BSB)

content: In Gideon's second fleece test, what happened?
explanation: Dew covered the ground instead. “Only the fleece was dry, and dew covered the ground.” (Judges 6:40, BSB)

content: When Gideon let the fearful go home, how many remained?
explanation: Twenty-two thousand turned back. “So twenty-two thousand of them turned back, but ten thousand remained.” (Judges 7:3, BSB)

content: How did God choose Gideon's three hundred at the water?
explanation: Those who lapped were kept. “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.” (Judges 7:5, BSB)

content: What did Manoah's wife name the son the angel promised her?
explanation: The LORD blessed the boy. “So the woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson.” (Judges 13:24, BSB)

content: What did Samson use to strike down a thousand Philistines?
explanation: God gave him strength. “He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.” (Judges 15:15, BSB)

content: How many braids of Samson's hair were shaved off?
explanation: Then his strength left him. “she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head.” (Judges 16:19, BSB)

content: When Samson woke after his hair was cut, what did he not know?
explanation: His strength was gone. “But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.” (Judges 16:20, BSB)

content: In prison in Gaza, what was Samson forced to do?
explanation: He was bound with bronze shackles. “and forced to grind grain in the prison.” (Judges 16:21, BSB)

content: In the Philistine temple, what did Samson ask God?
explanation: He prayed before pushing the pillars. “Strengthen me, O God, just once more” (Judges 16:28, BSB)

content: Who was the first deliverer God raised up in Judges, a relative of Caleb?
explanation: He was the son of Caleb's younger brother. “He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.” (Judges 3:9, BSB)

content: Which deliverer in Judges was a left-handed Benjamite?
explanation: He was sent to Eglon king of Moab. “He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer.” (Judges 3:15, BSB)

content: Sisera was the army commander of which king?
explanation: His army was drawn to the Kishon. “And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army” (Judges 4:7, BSB)

content: To which river did God draw Sisera's army in Deborah's day?
explanation: God delivered him to Barak. “his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon” (Judges 4:7, BSB)

content: Under the oak in which town did the angel find Gideon?
explanation: It belonged to Joash his father. “the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite” (Judges 6:11, BSB)

content: At what time of night did Gideon's men attack the Midianite camp?
options: The beginning of the middle watch
explanation: Just after the guard changed. “at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard.” (Judges 7:19, BSB)

content: Into how many companies did Gideon divide his three hundred men?
explanation: They surrounded the camp. “And he divided the three hundred men into three companies” (Judges 7:16, BSB)

content: What was the name of Samson's father?
explanation: He was a Danite from Zorah. “Now there was a man from Zorah named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites” (Judges 13:2, BSB)

content: Near which town's vineyards did a young lion attack Samson?
explanation: He tore it apart. “and came to the vineyards of Timnah. Suddenly a young lion came roaring at him” (Judges 14:5, BSB)

content: How much silver did each Philistine lord promise Delilah?
explanation: They wanted Samson's secret. “Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.” (Judges 16:5, BSB)

content: About how many people were on the roof of the Philistine temple watching Samson?
explanation: All the lords were there too. “and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.” (Judges 16:27, BSB)
